Logitech G510s Keyboard (with LCD Screen) is 36% off

I'm contemplating getting one, because I like the extra buttons. Have any of you used this?

Is the LCD screen just a gimmick?

I owned one of these and used it for a few years. The screen is not a gimmick. A lot of applications have a little applet that runs on it. My favorite was probably foobar2000. It had a "now playing" screen and a visualization. Some games had support of for it as well. Bad Company 2 let you see your kills, deaths and score without hitting tab. Civ V had some small lists that could be viewed on the screen, the best was probably the city overview which showed the overall production and consumption of your cities. I don't think a lot of games have any support though, so this is not really a selling point.

The function keys are useful, but I never needed the option to switch between three different sets if 18 functions. It was decent for writing your own scripts. I had an auto-click one for cookie clicker for a while, as well as an auto-mining one for Minecraft. I never used any scripts for competitive games, but the option is there if you want to be an asshole I guess.

The keys are not mechanical, but it is one of the best membrane keyboards I've used. the keys lasted quite well, and only a few keys started to wear after 2+ years of heavy use.

I actually got the most use out of the quick macros for programming and web-browsing. It was great to be able to have complex vim actions mapped to their own keys.

I ended up replacing this keyboard with a CODE mechanical keyboard because I liked the feeling of the mechanical switches for typing, but I do miss some of the functionality of the G510 when I game.

The problem as I see it is that The Name of the Wind frankly just isn't very good. It's a fun novel to read, but Kvothe is too much of a Gary Stue to succeed in a more passive environment like film. Audiences don't tend to respond favorably to protagonists who are amazing at everything, and while a favorite fan theory is that Kvothe is full of shit and an unreliable narrator, this would likely serve to confuse audiences.
It's also a bullshit cop-out to cover for bad narration and writing.

I don't see the appeal of making this into a movie. The plot and characters really aren't actually that good, the success lies mostly in the way it is written, which won't translate to the big screen. It'll result in a pretty generic fantasy movie with rampant comparisons to HP due to magic school.

With regard to Kvothe being good at everything he is actually portrayed as quite a klutz, at interpersonal relations.

And as far as being a good movie I think it could be a good action fantasy just by following the action narrative. Will it be as good as "Willow"? Probably not. But then nothing is.
